_about: Hand-written legal elements for the Bureau's most-used charges. These replace the auto-generated checklists from the penal code. Each element: text = what must be proven; proof = typical evidence that establishes it. Keyed by penal code number.

[2] 1.1.text: Identity — the suspect is the person who caused the victim's death.
[2] 1.1.proof: DNA/fingerprints on weapon, CCTV/bodycam, eyewitness ID, confession.
Coroner / Medical Examiner report, death confirmation on scene.

[2] 1.1.text: The suspect's act caused the death.
[2] 1.1.proof: ME cause of death matching the weapon or act; ballistics; scene reconstruction.

[2] 1.1.text: The killing was unlawful — not justified (e.g. self-defense) or excused.
[2] 1.1.proof: Witness statements, scene evidence and the suspect interview ruling out justification.
Nature of the attack (number/placement of wounds, weapon used), threats, statements.

[2] 1.1.text: The victim was a Law Enforcement Officer, active-duty military member or Federal Agent.
[2] 1.1.proof: Agency roster, uniform/badge, marked vehicle, dispatch records.

[2] 1.1.text: The victim was performing their lawful official duties at the time, OR was killed because of their official status.
[2] 1.1.proof: Dispatch/CAD logs, bodycam, radio traffic; statements showing motive tied to their role.

[2] 1.1.text: The suspect knew or reasonably should have known the victim's official status.
[2] 1.1.proof: Uniform, marked vehicle, lights/sirens, verbal identification, prior contact.

[2] 1.1.text: Charging check — not stacked with First or Second Degree Murder for the same victim and act.
[2] 1.1.proof: Review of charges on this case.

[2] 1.2.text: Identity — the suspect is the person who caused the victim's death.
[2] 1.2.proof: DNA/fingerprints on weapon, CCTV, eyewitness ID, phone location data, confession.

[2] 1.2.text: The suspect's act caused the death.
[2] 1.2.proof: ME cause of death consistent with the weapon or act; ballistics.

[2] 1.2.text: The killing was unlawful — not justified or excused.
[2] 1.2.proof: Witnesses, scene evidence, suspect interview ruling out self-defense.

[2] 1.2.text: The suspect intended to kill the victim.
[2] 1.2.proof: Weapon and manner of attack, threats, statements, wounds to vital areas.

[2] 1.2.text: Premeditation — the intent to kill was formed BEFORE the act (any length of time).
[2] 1.2.proof: Prior threats, messages, purchase of weapon, motive (financial, retaliation).

[2] 1.2.text: Deliberation — shown by planning, preparation, lying in wait, financial incentive, or other circumstances showing the killing was considered beforehand.
[2] 1.2.proof: Surveillance, travel to the location, bringing a weapon, contract/payment evidence, lying in wait.

[2] 1.2.text: Charging check — not stacked with Capital or Second Degree Murder for the same victim and act.
[2] 1.2.proof: Review of charges on this case.

[2] 1.3.text: Identity — the suspect is the person who caused the victim's death.
[2] 1.3.proof: DNA/fingerprints on weapon, CCTV, eyewitness ID, confession.

[2] 1.3.text: The suspect's act caused the death.
[2] 1.3.proof: ME cause of death consistent with the act or weapon.

[2] 1.3.text: The killing was unlawful — not justified or excused.
[2] 1.3.proof: Witnesses, scene evidence, suspect interview ruling out self-defense.

[2] 1.3.text: Malice — EITHER the suspect intended to kill, OR acted with a conscious disregard for human life (knew the act was extremely dangerous and did it anyway).
[2] 1.3.proof: Manner of attack, weapon used, statements; for disregard: shooting into a crowd, sustained beating.

[2] 1.3.text: No premeditation required — distinguishes from First Degree. Note facts showing a sudden or unplanned killing.
[2] 1.3.proof: Spontaneous confrontation, escalation, no prior planning found.

[2] 1.3.text: Charging check — not stacked with Capital or First Degree Murder for the same victim and act.
[2] 1.3.proof: Review of charges on this case.

[2] 1.4.text: Identity — the suspect is the person who made the attempt.
[2] 1.4.proof: Victim/witness ID, CCTV, DNA, shell casings matched to suspect's firearm.

[2] 1.4.text: Specific intent — the suspect intended to cause the victim's death.
[2] 1.4.proof: Threats, statements, aiming at vital areas, weapon choice, repeated attacks.

[2] 1.4.text: Direct and substantial step — the suspect went beyond preparation and acted toward killing the victim (e.g. fired at, stabbed, attempted to strangle).
[2] 1.4.proof: Shots fired, injuries, bodycam/CCTV of the attack, physical evidence.

[2] 1.4.text: The killing was not completed (the victim survived).
The attempt was unlawful — not justified or excused.
[2] 1.4.proof: Witnesses and scene evidence ruling out self-defense.

[2] 1.4.text: Charging check — if the victim later dies from this act, charge murder instead (do not stack).
[2] 1.4.proof: Victim's medical status at time of charging.

[2] 1.5.text: Identity — the suspect is the person who made the attempt.
Specific intent — the suspect intended to cause the officer's death.
[2] 1.5.proof: Firing at the officer, aiming at vital areas, statements/threats.

[2] 1.5.text: Direct and substantial step toward killing the officer (beyond preparation).
[2] 1.5.proof: Shots fired at officer, ramming, stabbing — bodycam, dashcam, damage to vehicle/vest.

[2] 1.5.text: The victim was a Law Enforcement Officer performing lawful official duties.
[2] 1.5.proof: Dispatch/CAD logs, call assignment, uniform and marked unit.

[2] 1.5.text: The suspect knew or reasonably should have known the victim was a Law Enforcement Officer.
[2] 1.5.proof: Uniform, marked vehicle, lights/sirens, verbal commands identifying police.

[2] 1.5.text: Charging check — not stacked with [2] 1.4 Attempted Murder for the same victim and act.
[2] 1.5.proof: Review of charges on this case.

[2] 2.text: Identity — the suspect was the driver of the vehicle.
[2] 2.proof: Witness ID, CCTV/dashcam, vehicle registration, DNA/prints on wheel or airbag, admission.

[2] 2.text: The suspect was operating a motor vehicle.
The driving was criminally negligent or reckless (a gross departure from careful driving — e.g. extreme speed, DUI, evading, red-light running).
[2] 2.proof: Speed estimates, crash reconstruction, toxicology/BAC, pursuit footage, witness statements.

[2] 2.text: The suspect's driving caused the death.
[2] 2.proof: Crash reconstruction, ME cause of death (vehicle-related trauma).

[2] 2.text: No intent to kill (if intent exists, charge murder instead).
Charging check — not stacked with Involuntary Manslaughter for the same death. Driver's license to be revoked.
[2] 2.proof: Review of charges on this case.

[2] 3.text: Identity — the suspect is the person whose conduct caused the death.
The suspect acted with criminal negligence or recklessness, OR committed an unlawful act creating a substantial and unjustifiable risk of death.
[2] 3.proof: Description of the dangerous act — e.g. unsafe firearm handling, dangerous assault, hazardous condition.

[2] 3.text: The suspect's conduct caused the death.
[2] 3.proof: ME cause of death linked to the conduct; scene reconstruction.

[2] 3.text: No intent to kill (if intent or conscious disregard exists, consider murder).
Charging check — if the death involved operating a motor vehicle, use Vehicular Manslaughter instead (do not stack).
[2] 3.proof: Review of charges on this case.

[1] 28.text: Identity — the suspect is the person who provided or sold the narcotics.
[1] 28.proof: Witnesses, messages arranging the deal, CCTV, CI information, phone records.

[1] 28.text: The suspect provided OR sold narcotics to the victim.
[1] 28.proof: Transaction evidence — messages, cash, witness to hand-off, packaging matching suspect's supply.

[1] 28.text: The victim consumed those specific narcotics.
[1] 28.proof: Drugs/paraphernalia found with victim, witness statements, toxicology.

[1] 28.text: Required — a Medical Examiner report links the cause of death to the narcotic (overdose, narcotic-induced cardiac arrest, etc.).
[1] 28.proof: ME report with cause of death and toxicology attached.

[1] 28.text: The narcotics that caused death are the same ones the suspect supplied.
[1] 28.proof: Lab match of substance/cut agent, packaging, timeline from purchase to death.

[7] 18.text: Identity — the suspect possessed, transported or distributed the contraband.
[7] 18.proof: Traffic stop/arrest, vehicle registration, CCTV, surveillance log, fingerprints on packaging.

[7] 18.text: The suspect transported, distributed or moved the contraband within the state.
[7] 18.proof: Vehicle stop, surveillance of movement, shipping/delivery evidence.

[7] 18.text: The items were illegal goods, contraband or controlled items (drugs, firearms, ammunition, explosives, alcohol or other regulated materials).
[7] 18.proof: Lab test of drugs, firearm/ammo inventory, photos of seized items.

[7] 18.text: The suspect knew the items were present and illegal (knowing possession or control).
[7] 18.proof: Items in suspect's vehicle/stash, statements, concealment, efforts to evade.

[7] 18.text: Quantity threshold met — ANY ONE of: 25 lb drugs/tobacco · 25 gal alcohol · 25 firearms · 25 magazines · 250 rounds · 5 lb explosives — OR ANY TWO of: 15 lb drugs/tobacco · 15 gal alcohol · 15 firearms · 15 magazines · 100 rounds · 3 lb explosives.
[7] 18.proof: Weighed and counted evidence inventory with photos; record exact totals.

[7] 18.text: No direct evidence of a border crossing (if there is, charge [11] 5 Smuggling instead). BUREAU POLICY: firearms/weapons trafficking is charged under [11] 5 Smuggling, not this charge. Does not apply to transporting persons.
[7] 18.proof: Origin of the shipment / route; type of contraband.

[7] 7.text: Identity — the suspect is the person who distributed the substance.
[7] 7.proof: Undercover/CI buy, surveillance, CCTV, messages, marked money.

[7] 7.text: The suspect sold or distributed a controlled substance.
[7] 7.proof: Controlled buy, observed hand-to-hand transactions, messages arranging sales.

[7] 7.text: The substance was an illicit controlled substance, OR a prescription substance distributed outside what [7] 6 permits.
Required — probable cause that the substance was packaged in bindles / prepared for sale, OR that the sale was attracting a large number of people in a way clearly indicating distribution.
[7] 7.proof: Photos of packaging, scales, baggies; surveillance of foot traffic.

[7] 8.text: Identity — the suspect possessed the substance.
The suspect knowingly possessed a controlled substance (in violation of [7] 6).
[7] 8.proof: Location of drugs, control of the area, statements.

[7] 8.text: The substance is a controlled substance.
Quantity — 5 ounces or more of a controlled substance.
[7] 8.proof: Weighed evidence with photo of scale reading.

[7] 8.text: Intent to distribute — supporting indicators (scales, baggies, large sums of cash, burner phones, scent-masking items, large amounts of paraphernalia).
[7] 8.proof: Photos and inventory of indicators seized.

[11] 30.text: Identity — the suspect manufactured, transported or sold the product.
[11] 30.proof: Presence at lab/facility, surveillance, purchase records for precursors, fingerprints/DNA on equipment.

[11] 30.text: MANUFACTURE — the suspect manufactured an illicit substance, OR manufactured a prescription substance / alcohol / tobacco product without the required permits, licenses and operating requirements.
[11] 30.proof: Lab equipment, precursor chemicals, product in production, licensing records check.

[11] 30.text: OR TRANSPORT — the suspect knowingly transported an illegally produced controlled substance, alcohol or tobacco product (lawful cannabis transport excepted).
OR SALE — the suspect knowingly sold an illegally produced product, or sold without the licenses required by law.
Knowledge — the suspect knew the product was illegally produced (for transport/sale) or was knowingly operating the manufacturing.
[11] 30.proof: Statements, role in the operation, concealment, cash handling.

[11] 30.text: No valid license/permit covers the activity (including cannabis outside state license or personal limits).
Federal charge — coordinate with federal authorities as required.

[2] 5.text: Identity — the suspect took or held the victim.
[2] 5.proof: Victim ID, witnesses, CCTV, vehicle registration, phone location data.

[2] 5.text: The suspect took, held or abducted the victim.
[2] 5.proof: Victim statement, witnesses, bodycam, restraints found.

[2] 5.text: The suspect moved the victim a substantial distance, and/or held them for an extended period of time.
[2] 5.proof: Start and end locations, timeline, GPS/phone data, CCTV along the route.
Victim statement, signs of struggle, restraints, calls for help.

[2] 5.text: By force or fear — physical force was actually used on the victim, OR imminent physical harm was threatened.
[2] 5.proof: Injuries/medical report, weapon displayed, threats heard by witnesses or recorded.

[2] 5.text: Classification — felony or federal depending on the nature of the victim (e.g. government officials/federal victims). Record which applies.

[2] 6.text: Identity — the suspect held the hostage.
[2] 6.proof: Negotiation recordings, bodycam, witness and hostage statements.

[2] 6.text: The suspect restrained, confined or detained a person without their consent.
With a threat against the person's life or well-being.
[2] 6.proof: Weapon held to hostage, recorded threats, negotiator logs.

[2] 6.text: With intent or declaration to use the person for leverage — escape, protection from arrest (human shield), or personal gain.
[2] 6.proof: Demands made, negotiation transcript, use as shield on bodycam.

[2] 6.text: Defenses ruled out — no consent and there was an imminent threat of arrest or other leverage purpose.

[2] 4.text: Identity — the suspect restrained the victim.
The suspect intentionally restrained, confined or detained the victim.
Against the victim's will, in a way that substantially interfered with their freedom of movement.
[2] 4.proof: Duration and manner of confinement, attempts to leave.

[2] 4.text: Without lawful authority, legal justification or consent (not lawful arrest, self-defense, shopkeeper's privilege or appropriate parental rights).

[11] 5.text: Identity — the suspect transported or harbored the items or persons.
[11] 5.proof: Vessel/aircraft/vehicle ownership or operation, port/airfield footage, admission.

[11] 5.text: The suspect transported or harbored weapons, firearms, ammunition, explosives, drugs/controlled substances, narcotics, tobacco, alcohol, or currency over $10,000 — OR a person whose entry was being concealed.
[11] 5.proof: Seized items inventory, photos, cash count; person found concealed.

[11] 5.text: Into the State of San Andreas — evidence of a border crossing (by sea, air or land). BUREAU POLICY: firearms/weapons trafficking within the state is also charged under [11] 5; if so, record here that this is an in-state firearms trafficking case and the quantities involved.
[11] 5.proof: Border crossing: boat/aircraft tracking, arrival from outside the state, port logs. In-state firearms trafficking: seized firearm/ammo inventory with counts, route/surveillance, transaction evidence.

[11] 5.text: The items were not lawful to possess, or were not declared for inspection before entry.
The suspect knew the items/persons were being brought in.
[11] 5.proof: Concealment efforts, statements, role in the operation, communications.

[11] 5.text: Federal charge — coordinate with federal authorities as required. For in-state DRUG or other non-firearm trafficking without a border crossing, use [7] 18 Trafficking.

[11] 31.text: Identity — the suspect manufactured, transported or sold the weapons.
[11] 31.proof: Presence at workshop, surveillance, fingerprints/DNA on tools or parts, purchase records.

[11] 31.text: MANUFACTURE — the suspect manufactured, assembled or produced an illegal weapon, OR manufactured firearms/ammunition as a business without a federal license, OR knowingly operated or materially assisted an unlawful manufacturing operation.
[11] 31.proof: Workshop with tools, 3D printers, jigs, parts kits, unfinished frames, ammunition press; license check.

[11] 31.text: OR TRANSPORT — the suspect knowingly transported, shipped or distributed unlawfully made or prohibited firearms, weapons, ammunition, parts, modifications or kits.
OR SALE — the suspect knowingly sold or transferred unlawfully made or prohibited weapons, ammunition, parts, modifications or kits.
[11] 31.proof: Controlled buy, CI information, transaction messages, cash.

[11] 31.text: Knowledge — the suspect knew the weapons were unlawfully made or prohibited.
[11] 31.proof: No serial numbers, conversion devices, statements, concealment.

[11] 31.text: Federal charge — coordinate with federal authorities. For a one-off individual sale (no manufacturing/commercial operation) use [8] 5 Illegal Sale of Weapon.

[8] 5.text: Identity — the suspect sold, traded, transferred or delivered the weapon.
[8] 5.proof: Controlled buy, CI information, messages, CCTV, marked money.

[8] 5.text: The suspect sold, traded, transferred, delivered or distributed a firearm, weapon or ammunition.
[8] 5.proof: Transaction evidence — hand-off observed, payment records, messages.

[8] 5.text: The transfer was unlawful because AT LEAST ONE applies: (a) the weapon is an illegal class under [8] 7; (b) the buyer lacked the required license; (c) the buyer was legally prohibited (suspect knew); (d) the suspect was dealing without a dealer license; or (e) the deal was arranged to avoid licensing/transfer rules.
[8] 5.proof: Weapon classification, buyer's license and criminal history check, dealer license check.

[8] 5.text: Knowledge — where required (prohibited buyer, avoiding requirements), the suspect knew the transfer was unlawful.
[8] 5.proof: Messages, statements, cash-only/no-paperwork deal, removed serial numbers.
